taskDescription: Complete the crossword using key terms from PA H1 | Hematopoiesis & Blood Specimen Basics. All clues relate to blood cell production, bone marrow biology, and growth factors essential for understanding the haematopoietic system.

words.clue: The continuous process by which all blood cells are produced from stem cells in the bone marrow.
Hormone produced by the kidney that stimulates red blood cell production in response to hypoxia.
Growth factor produced by liver and kidney that drives megakaryopoiesis and platelet production.
Immature red blood cell with residual ribonucleic acid mesh visible on supravital staining.
The most prolific blood cell lineage that generates two million new cells per second in healthy adults.
Oxygen-carrying protein that progressively accumulates in cytoplasm during polychromatic stage of red cell maturation.
Intermediate cell that undergoes commitment and can develop into specific blood cell types.
Common progenitor cell that gives rise to red cells, platelets, neutrophils, and monocytes.
Common progenitor cell that gives rise to T cells, B cells, and natural killer cells.
Specific developmental pathway or fate determined by transcription factors after progenitor cell commitment.
